source.author: verg
source.text: infelix pugnae iuvenem in certamine credit exstinctum et, subito mentem turbata dolore, se causam clamat crimenque caputque malorum, multaque per maestum demens effata furorem purpureos moritura manu discindit amictus et nodum informis leti trabe nectit ab alta.
source.text_original: infelix pugnae iuvenem in certamine credit / exstinctum et, subito mentem turbata dolore, / se causam clamat crimenque caputque malorum, / multaque per maestum demens effata furorem / purpureos moritura manu discindit amictus / et nodum informis leti trabe nectit ab alta.
source.text_english: Unhappy, in the contest she believes the youth has been killed, and, suddenly mind confounded by grief, she cries that she is the cause, the guilt, and the source of their troubles; and, in her madness, having uttered many things in her sorrowful frenzy, she tears her purple robe with her hand, and, about to die, she knots the noose of hideous death from a high beam.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: ludas, qui quondam audierat: tu autem, homo, dux meus et notus meus; in domo dei ambulauimus cum consensu, proditor amici, magistri, saluatoris arguitur et nodum informis leti trabe nectit ab alta.
reuse.text_original: ludas, qui quondam audierat: tu autem, homo, dux meus et notus meus; in domo dei ambulauimus cum consensu, proditor amici, magistri, saluatoris arguitur et nodum informis leti trabe nectit ab alta.
reuse.text_english: You are playing the part of Judas, who once heard: but you, man, my guide and my familiar friend; we walked in the house of God with agreement. He is accused as a traitor to a friend, a teacher, a savior, and from a high beam he ties the knot of a shapeless death.
